newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer did not suggest EMU delay - Bundesbank.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer did not suggest EMU delay - Bundesbank.

text.p: Germany's Bundesbank said on Saturday its president Hans Tietmeyer had not suggested delaying the planned 1999 start of Europe's monetary union (EMU).

Deputy spokesman Wolf-Ruediger Bengs told Reuters that Tietmeyer had not spoken since March with Der Spiegel magazine, which reported on Saturday that he had asked whether Germany and France could delay the euro because of difficulties in meeting criteria for it.
"It is wrong," Bengs said of the Spiegel report, without saying whether Tietmeyer might have made the comment on another occasion. "Tietmayer has not suggested to delay the monetary union."
Spiegel, quoting its own sources, said Tietmeyer had raised the possibility of a Franco-German initiative to delay EMU.
According to the magazine, he also said it would not be a catastrophe if Germany, now struggling to meet the strict Maastrict budget deficit criteria for EMU, went over the target this year.
Finance Minister Theo Waigel rejected any talk of delaying the start of the EMU.
